title: Brute Force
description: Adversaries may use brute force to gain access to accounts by guessing passwords or otherwise repeatedly testing authentication material.
guidance: Correlate authentication failures by source, account, and time window. Treat the pattern as suspicious behavior, not proof of compromise.

title: Password Guessing
description: Adversaries may guess passwords for accounts, including by trying common or likely passwords against an authentication service.
guidance: Review the event sequence and affected accounts. A successful login after failures is evidence of access, but does not alone establish malicious intent or impact.

title: Valid Accounts
description: Adversaries may obtain and abuse existing account credentials to gain access to systems or services.
guidance: Only associate this behavior when records show use of an existing account. Do not infer account compromise from failed authentication attempts alone.

title: SSH Authentication Attack Investigation
description: A focused review of SSH authentication events can identify repeated failures, invalid-user attempts, and successful logins in context.
guidance: Preserve raw event records, correlate timestamps and source addresses, distinguish invalid-user attempts from failures for known accounts, and verify any success against the stored event.

title: Credential Attack Containment
description: Containment should reduce exposure while preserving evidence and avoiding actions unsupported by the investigation.
guidance: For human review, consider confirming affected accounts, rotating credentials when authorized, reviewing SSH access policy, and preserving relevant logs. Do not block or modify systems automatically based only on a detection.
